PE1-01.hint: The graph of a quadratic function is a parabola, and this one opens downward, so the maximum is at the vertex. The vertex is at \(t = -\dfrac{b}{2a}\). The height is the output, so put that time back into \(H\).
slips: Stopping at the time. Part (b) asks for a height, which is an output of \(H\), not the input \(2.5\).
Losing the negative sign in \(-\dfrac{b}{2a}\). Here \(a = -16\), so the denominator is negative and the two negatives cancel.
Leaving off units. Time is in seconds and height is in feet.
PE1-01.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

PE1-02.hint: This parabola opens upward, so the vertex is a minimum. Find the vertex input with \(-\dfrac{b}{2a}\), then evaluate \(C\) there for the cost.
slips: Using \(b = 100\) instead of \(b = -100\). The sign of \(b\) matters.
Giving \(125\) as the minimum cost. \(125\) is the number of units (the input); the cost is the output.
Leaving off units or the dollar sign.
PE1-02.source: Practice Exam 1 review (the 38 questions on the Exam 1 review site, 172exam1review)

items.stem: A ball is thrown upward. Its height after \(t\) seconds is \(H(t) = -16t^{2} + 80t\), in feet.

parts.q: At what time is the height a maximum?

items.stem: The cost, in dollars, to produce \(x\) units is \(C(x) = 0.4x^{2} - 100x + 8500\).

parts.q: How many units minimize the cost?
